text:
Planes fly because of the shape of their wings. Air moves faster over the top of the wing and slower underneath. This creates a difference in pressure, which generates lift.

Lift is the upward force that counteracts gravity. Gravity pulls the plane down, but as long as lift is stronger, the plane rises.

The engines provide thrust, pushing the plane forward. Forward motion helps maintain airflow over the wings, keeping lift steady.

By balancing lift, thrust, gravity, and drag, pilots can control the plane’s movement in the air. That’s how planes stay up and safely travel through the sky.
